newsitem.title: UGANDA: European aid for Uganda's fish exports.
newsitem.headline: European aid for Uganda's fish exports.

text.p: The European Development Fund is giving Uganda $34 million to modernise cargo facilities at Entebbe airport to boost exports of freshwater fish, now Uganda's second-biggest currency earner, officials said on Sunday.
Only coffee, the country's main export crop, earns more than fish.
Civil Aviation Authority managing director Ambrose Nkandonda said the grant would finance a cold-storage facility and related extension work.
"Fish exports to Europe have risen sharply, and the absence of an airport cold storage facility has raised fears of bacterial contamination of shipments," he said.
The European Union has said that imports of Ugandan fish could be banned if handling facilities were not improved.
Uganda Fish Exporters Association Philip Borel said: "We are facing a major crisis if a cold storage facility is not quickly provided."

Fishing, mainly from Lake Victoria -- Africa's largest lake -- produces up to 220,000 tonnes of fish a year. The industry employs about 60,000 people directly and up to 500,000 indirectly, trade experts said.
Fish exports earn Uganda about $50 million a year.
